قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿اسْتَطْعَما أهْلَها﴾؛ أيْ: سَألاهُمُ الضِّيافَةَ، ﴿فَأبَوْا أنْ يُضَيِّفُوهُما﴾. رَوى المُفَضَّلُ عَنْ عاصِمٍ: ( يُضَيِّفُوهُما ) بِضَمِّ الياءِ الأُولى وكَسْرِ الضّادِ وتَخْفِيفِ الياءِ الثّانِيَةِ. وقَرَأ أبُو الجَوْزاءِ كَذَلِكَ، إلّا أنَّهُ فَتَحَ الياءَ [الأُولى]. وقَرَأ الباقُونَ: ( يُضَيِّفُوهُما ) بِفَتْحِ الضّادِ وتَشْدِيدِ الياءِ الثّانِيَةِ وكَسْرِها. قالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: ومَعْنى ﴿يُضَيِّفُوهُما﴾: يُنْزِلُوهُما مَنزِلَ الأضْيافِ، يُقالُ: ضِفْتُ أنا، وأضافَنِي الَّذِي يُنْزِلُنِي. وقالَ الزَّجّاجُ: يُقالُ: ضِفْتُ الرَّجُلَ: إذا نَزَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ، وأضَفْتُهُ: إذا أنْزَلْتُهُ وقَرَيْتُهُ. وقالَ ابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ: [يُقالُ]: ضَيَّفْتُ الرَّجُلَ: إذا أنْزَلْتُهُ مَنزِلَةَ الأضْيافِ، ومِنهُ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ، وأضَفْتُهُ: أنْزَلْتُهُ، وضِفْتُهُ: نَزَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ. ورَوى أُبَيُّ بْنُ كَعْبٍ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللهِ (ﷺ)، قالَ: «كانُوا أهْلَ قَرْيَةٍ لِئامًا».

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَوَجَدا فِيها جِدارًا﴾؛ أيْ: حائِطًا. قالَ ابْنُ فارِسٍ: وجَمْعُهُ جُدُرٌ، والجُدُرُ: أصْلُ الحائِطِ. ومِنهُ حَدِيثُ الزُّبَيْرِ: «ثُمَّ دَعِ الماءَ يَرْجِعُ إلى الجَدْرِ»، والجَيْدَرُ: القَصِيرُ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿يُرِيدُ أنْ يَنْقَضَّ﴾. وقَرَأ أُبَيُّ بْنُ كَعْبٍ وأبُو رَجاءٍ: ( يَنْقاضُ ) بِألِفٍ مَمْدُودَةٍ وضادٍ مُعْجَمَةٍ. وقَرَأ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، وأبُو العالِيَةِ، وأبُو عُثْمانَ النَّهْدِيُّ: ( يَنْقاصُ ) بِألِفٍ ومَدَّةٍ وصادٍ غَيْرِ مُعْجَمَةٍ، وكُلُّهُ بِلا تَشْدِيدٍ. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: فَمَعْنى يَنْقُضُ: يَسْقُطُ بِسُرْعَةٍ، ويَنْقاصُ غَيْرُ مُعْجَمَةٍ: يَنْشَقُّ طُولًا، يُقالُ: انْقاصَتْ سِنُّهُ: إذا انْشَقَّتْ. قالَ ابْنُ مُقْسِمٍ: انْقاصَتْ سِنُّهُ، وانْقاضَتْ - بِالصّادِ والضّادِ - عَلى مَعْنًى واحِدٍ.

فَإنْ قِيلَ: كَيْفَ نُسِبَتِ الإرادَةُ إلى ما لا يَعْقِلُ؟

فالجَوابُ: أنَّ هَذا عَلى وجْهِ المَجازِ تَشْبِيهًا بِمَن يَعْقِلُ، ويُرِيدُ: لِأنَّ هَيْأتَهُ في التَّهَيُّؤِ لِلْوُقُوعِ قَدْ ظَهَرَتْ كَما يَظْهَرُ مِن أفْعالِ المُرِيدِينَ القاصِدِينَ، فَوُصِفَ بِالإرادَةِ؛ إذْ كانَتِ الصُّورَتانِ واحِدَةً، وقَدْ أضافَتِ العَرَبُ الأفْعالَ إلى ما لا يَعْقِلُ تَجَوُّزًا، قالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وجَلَّ: ﴿وَلَمّا سَكَتَ عَنْ مُوسى الغَضَبُ﴾ [الأعْرافِ: ١٥٤]، والغَضَبُ لا يَسْكُتُ، وإنَّما يَسْكُتُ صاحِبُهُ، وقالَ: ﴿فَإذا عَزَمَ الأمْرُ﴾ [مُحَمَّدٍ: ٢١]، وأنْشَدُوا مِن ذَلِكَ:

إنَّ دَهْرًا يَلُفُّ شَمْلِي بِجُمَلٍ ∗∗∗ لِزَمانٍ يَهُمُّ بِالإحْسانِ

وَقالَ آخَرُ:

يُرِيدُ الرُّمْحُ صَدْرَ أبِي بَراءٍ ∗∗∗ ويَرْغَبُ عَنْ دِماءِ بَنِي عَقِيلِ

وَقالَ آخَرُ:

ضَحِكُوا والدَّهْرُ عَنْهم ساكِتٌ ∗∗∗ ثُمَّ أبْكاهم دَمًا لَمّا نَطَقَ

وَقالَ آخَرُ:

يَشْكُو إلَيَّ جَمَلِي طُولَ السَّرى ∗∗∗ صَبْرًا جَمِيلًا فَكِلانا مُبْتَلى

وَهَذا كَثِيرٌ في أشْعارِهِمْ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَأقامَهُ﴾؛ أيْ: سَوّاهُ؛ لِأنَّهُ وجَدَهُ مائِلًا.

وَفِي كَيْفِيَّةِ ما فَعَلَ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ دَفَعَهُ بِيَدِهِ فَقامَ. والثّانِي: هَدَمَهُ ثُمَّ قَعَدَ يَبْنِيهِ، رُوِيَ القَوْلانِ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لَوْ شِئْتَ لاتَّخَذْتَ عَلَيْهِ أجْرًا﴾. قَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ وأبُو عَمْرٍو: ( لَتَخِذْتَ ) بِكَسْرِ الخاءِ، غَيْرَ أنَّ أبا عَمْرٍو كانَ يُدْغِمُ الذّالَ، وابْنُ كَثِيرٍ يُظْهِرُها. وقَرَأ نافِعٌ، وعاصِمٌ، وابْنُ عامِرٍ، وحَمْزَةُ، والكِسائِيُّ: ( لاتَّخَذْتَ ) وكُلُّهم أدْغَمُوا، إلّا حَفْصًا عَنْ عاصِمٍ، فَإنَّهُ لَمْ يُدْغِمْ مِثْلَ ابْنِ كَثِيرٍ. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: يُقالُ: تَخِذَ يَتَّخِذُ في مَعْنى: اتَّخَذَ يَتَّخِذُ. وإنَّما قالَ لَهُ هَذا؛ لِأنَّهم لَمْ يُضَيِّفُوهُما.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿قالَ﴾ يَعْنِي: الخَضِرَ، ﴿هَذا﴾ يَعْنِي: الإنْكارَ عَلَيَّ، ﴿فِراقُ بَيْنِي وبَيْنِكَ﴾؛ أيْ: هو المُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَنا. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: المَعْنى: هَذا فِراقٌ بَيْنِنا؛ أيْ: فِراقُ اتِّصالِنا، وكَرَّرَ ( بَيْنَ ) تَوْكِيدًا، ومِثْلُهُ في الكَلامِ: أخْزى اللَّهُ الكاذِبَ مِنِّي ومِنكَ. وقَرَأ أبُو رَزِينٍ، وابْنُ السَّمَيْفَعِ، وأبُو العالِيَةِ، وابْنُ أبِي عَبْلَةَ: ( هَذا فِراقٌ ) بِالتَّنْوِينِ ( بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكَ ) بِنَصْبِ النُّونِ. قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: كانَ قَوْلُ مُوسى في السَّفِينَةِ والغُلامِ لِرَبِّهِ، وكانَ قَوْلُهُ في الجِدارِ لِنَفْسِهِ، لِطَلَبِ شَيْءٍ مِن الدُّنْيا.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَلا تَسْألْنِي﴾ قَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ، وأبُو عَمْرٍو، وعاصِمٌ، وحَمْزَةُ، والكِسائِيُّ: ( فَلا تَسْألْنِي ) ساكِنَةَ اللّامِ. وقَرَأ نافِعٌ: ( فَلا تَسْألْنِي ) مَفْتُوحَةَ اللّامِ مُشَدَّدَةَ النُّونِ. وقَرَأ ابْنُ عامِرٍ في رِوايَةِ الدّاجُونِيِّ: ( فَلا تَسْألْنِ عَنْ شَيْءٍ ) بِتَحْرِيكِ اللّامِ مِن غَيْرِ ياءٍ والنُّونُ مَكْسُورَةٌ، والمَعْنى: لا تَسْألْنِي عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِمّا أفْعَلُهُ، ﴿حَتّى أُحْدِثَ لَكَ مِنهُ ذِكْرًا﴾؛ أيْ: حَتّى أكُونَ أنا الَّذِي أُبَيِّنُهُ لَكَ؛ لِأنَّ عِلْمَهُ قَدْ غابَ عَنْكَ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿خَرَقَها﴾؛ أيْ: شَقَّها. قالَ المُفَسِّرُونَ: قَلَعَ مِنها لَوْحًا، وقِيلَ: لَوْحَيْنِ مِمّا يَلِي الماءَ، فَحَشاها مُوسى بِثَوْبِهِ، وأنْكَرَ عَلَيْهِ ما فَعَلَ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿أخَرَقْتَها لِتُغْرِقَ أهْلَها﴾. قَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ، ونافِعٌ، وأبُو عَمْرٍو، وعاصِمٌ، وابْنُ عامِرٍ: ( لِتُغْرِقَ ) بِالتّاءِ ( أهْلَها ) بِالنَّصْبِ. وقَرَأ حَمْزَةُ والكِسائِيُّ: ( لِيَغْرَقَ ) بِالياءِ ( أهْلُها ) بِرَفْعِ اللّامِ. ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئًا إمْرًا﴾ وفِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ أقْوالٍ:

أحَدُها: مُنْكَرًا، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ. وقالَ الزَّجّاجُ: عَظِيمًا مِنَ المُنْكَرِ. والثّانِي: عَجَبًا، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ وابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ. والثّالِثُ: داهِيَةً، قالَهُ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لا تُؤاخِذْنِي بِما نَسِيتُ﴾ في هَذا النِّسْيانِ ثَلاثَةُ أقْوالٍ:

أحَدُها: أنَّهُ عَلى حَقِيقَتِهِ وأنَّهُ نَسِيَ، رَوى ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللهِ (ﷺ) «أنَّ الأُولى كانَتْ نِسْيانًا مِن مُوسى».

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ لَمْ يَنْسَ، ولَكِنَّهُ مِن مَعارِيضِ الكَلامِ، قالَهُ أُبَيُّ بْنُ كَعْبٍ وابْنُ عَبّاسٍ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ بِمَعْنى التَّرْكِ، فالمَعْنى: لا تُؤاخِذْنِي بِما تَرَكْتَهُ مِمّا عاهَدْتُكَ عَلَيْهِ، ذَكَرَهُ ابْنُ الأنْبارِيِّ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَلا تُرْهِقْنِي﴾ قالَ الفَرّاءُ: لا تُعَجِّلْنِي. وقالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ، وابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ، والزَّجّاجُ: لا تَغُشَّنِي. قالَ أبُو زَيْدٍ: يُقالُ: أرْهَقْتُهُ عُسْرًا: إذا كَلَّفْتَهُ ذَلِكَ. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: والمَعْنى: عامِلْنِي بِاليُسْرِ لا بِالعُسْرِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فانْطَلَقا﴾ يَعْنِي: مُوسى والخَضِرَ. قالَ الماوَرْدِيُّ: يُحْتَمَلُ أنَّ يُوشَعَ تَأخَّرَ عَنْهُما؛ لِأنَّ الإخْبارَ عَنِ اثْنَيْنِ، ويُحْتَمَلُ أنْ يَكُونَ مَعَهُما ولَمْ يُذْكَرْ؛ لِأنَّهُ تَبِعٌ لِمُوسى، فاقْتَصَرَ عَلى حُكْمِ المَتْبُوعِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿حَتّى إذا لَقِيا غُلامًا﴾ اخْتَلَفُوا في هَذا الغُلامِ، هَلْ كانَ بالِغًا أمْ لا؟ عَلى قَوْلَيْنِ:

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ بالِغًا، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، ومُجاهِدٌ، والأكْثَرُونَ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ كانَ شابًّا قَدْ قَبَضَ عَلى لِحْيَتِهِ، حَكاهُ الماوَرْدِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا، واحْتَجَّ بِأنَّ غَيْرَ البالِغِ لَمْ يَجْرِ عَلَيْهِ قَلَمٌ، فَلَمْ يَسْتَحِقَّ القَتْلَ. وقَدْ يُسَمّى الرَّجُلُ غُلامًا، قالَتْ لَيْلى الأخْيَلِيَّةُ تَمْدَحُ الحَجّاجَ:

شَفاها مِن الدّاءِ العُضالِ الَّذِي بِها ∗∗∗ غُلامٌ إذا هَزَّ القَناةَ سَقاها

وَفِي صِفَةِ قَتْلِهِ لَهُ ثَلاثَةُ أقْوالٍ:

أحَدُها: أنَّهُ اقْتَلَعَ رَأْسَهُ، وقَدْ ذَكَرْناهُ في حَدِيثِ أُبَيٍّ. والثّانِي: كَسَرَ عُنُقَهُ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ. والثّالِثُ: أضْجَعَهُ وذَبَحَهُ بِالسِّكِّينِ، قالَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ( أقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا زاكِيَةً ) قَرَأ الكُوفِيُّونَ وابْنُ عامِرٍ: ( ﴿زَكِيَّةً﴾ ) بِغَيْرِ ألِفٍ والياءُ مُشَدَّدَةٌ. وقَرَأ الباقُونَ بِالألِفٍ مِن غَيْرِ تَشْدِيدٍ. قالَ الكِسائِيُّ: هُما لُغَتانِ بِمَعْنًى واحِدٍ، وهُما بِمَنزِلَةِ القاسِيَةِ والقَسِيَّةِ.

وَلِلْمُفَسِّرِينَ فِيها سِتَّةُ أقْوالٍ:

أحَدُها: أنَّها التّائِبَةُ، رُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أنَّهُ قالَ: الزَّكِيَّةُ: التّائِبَةُ، [وبِهِ] قالَ الضَّحّاكُ.

والثّانِي: أنَّها المُسْلِمَةُ، رُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّها الزَّكِيَّةُ الَّتِي لَمْ تَبْلُغْ الخَطايا، قالَهُ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ.

والرّابِعُ: أنَّها الزَّكِيَّةُ النّامِيَةُ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ. وقالَ ابْنُ الأنْبارِيِّ: القَوِيمَةُ في تَرْكِيبِها.

والخامِسُ: أنَّ الزَّكِيَّةَ: المُطَهَّرَةُ، قالَهُ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ.

والسّادِسُ: أنَّ الزَّكِيَّةَ: البَرِيئَةُ الَّتِي لَمْ يَظْهَرْ ما يُوجِبُ قَتْلَها، قالَهُ الزَّجّاجُ.

وَقَدْ فَرَّقَ بَعْضُهم بَيْنَ الزّاكِيَةِ والزَّكِيَّةِ، فَرُوِيَ عَنْ أبِي عَمْرٍو بْنِ العَلاءِ أنَّهُ قالَ: الزّاكِيَةُ: الَّتِي لَمْ تُذْنِبْ قَطُّ، والزَّكِيَّةُ: الَّتِي أذْنَبَتْ ثُمَّ تابَتْ. ورُوِيَ عَنْ أبِي عُبَيْدَةَ أنَّهُ قالَ: الزّاكِيَةُ في البَدَنِ، والزَّكِيَّةُ في الدِّينِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ﴾؛ أيْ: بِغَيْرِ قَتْلِ نَفْسٍ، ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئًا نُكْرًا﴾. قَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ، وأبُو عَمْرٍو، وحَمْزَةُ، والكِسائِيُّ: ( نُكْرًا ) خَفِيفَةً في كُلِّ القُرْآنِ، إلّا قَوْلُهُ: ﴿إلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ﴾ [القَمَرِ: ٦]، وخَفَّفَ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ أيْضًا ( إلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ ). وقَرَأ ابْنُ عامِرٍ وأبُو بَكْرٍ عَنْ عاصِمٍ: ( نُكُرًا ) و( إلى شَيْءٍ نُكْرٍ ) مُثْقَلٍ. والمُخَفَّفُ إنَّما هو مِنَ المُثَقَّلِ، كالعُنْقِ والعُنُقِ، والنُّكْرِ والنُّكُرِ. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: والمَعْنى: لَقَدْ أتَيْتَ شَيْئًا نُكُرًا. ويَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ مَعْناهُ: جِئْتَ بِشَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ، فَلَمّا حَذَفَ الباءَ أفْضى الفِعْلُ فَنَصَبَ نُكْرًا. و﴿نُكْرًا﴾ أقَلُّ مُنْكَرًا مِن قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إمْرًا﴾؛ لِأنَّ تَغْرِيقَ مَن في السَّفِينَةِ كانَ عِنْدَهُ أنْكَرُ مِن قَتْلِ نَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿قالَ ألَمْ أقُلْ لَكَ﴾.

إنْ قِيلَ: لِمَ ذَكَرَ ﴿لَكَ﴾ هاهُنا واخْتَزَلَهُ مِنَ المَوْضِعِ الَّذِي قَبْلَهُ؟

فالجَوابُ: أنَّ إثْباتَهُ لِلتَّوْكِيدِ واخْتِزالَهُ لِوُضُوحِ المَعْنى، وكِلاهُما مَعْرُوفٌ عِنْدَ الفُصَحاءِ. تَقُولُ العَرَبُ: قَدْ قُلْتُ لَكَ: اتَّقِ اللَّهَ، وقَدْ قُلْتُ لَكَ: يا فُلانُ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ، وأنْشَدَ ثَعْلَبُ:

قَدْ كُنْتُ حَذَّرْتُكَ آلَ المُصْطَلِقِ ∗∗∗ وقُلْتُ يا هَذا أطِعْنِي وانْطَلِقْ

فَقَوْلُهُ: يا هَذا، تَوْكِيدٌ لا يَخْتَلُّ الكَلامُ بِسُقُوطِهِ. وسَمِعْتُ الشَّيْخَ أبا مُحَمَّدٍ الخَشّابَ يَقُولُ: وقَّرَهُ في الأوَّلِ، فَلَمْ يُواجِهْهُ بِكافِ الخِطابِ، فَلَمّا خالَفَ في الثّانِي واجَهَهُ بِها.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿إنْ سَألْتُكَ عَنْ شَيْءٍ﴾؛ أيْ: سُؤالُ تَوْبِيخٍ وإنْكارٍ، ﴿بَعْدَها﴾؛ أيْ: بَعْدَ هَذِهِ المَسْألَةِ، ﴿فَلا تُصاحِبْنِي﴾. وقَرَأ كَذَلِكَ مُعاذٌ القارِئُ، وأبُو نَهِيِكٍ، وأبُو المُتَوَكِّلِ، والأعْرَجُ، إلّا أنَّهم شَدَّدُوا النُّونَ. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: ومَعْناهُ: إنْ طَلَبْتُ صُحْبَتَكَ فَلا تُتابِعْنِي عَلى ذَلِكَ. وقَرَأ أُبَيُّ بْنُ كَعْبٍ، وابْنُ أبِي عَبْلَةَ، ويَعْقُوبُ: ( فَلا تَصْحَبْنِي ) بِفَتْحِ التّاءِ مِن غَيْرِ ألِفٍ. وقَرَأ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، وأبُو العالِيَةِ، والأعْمَشُ كَذَلِكَ، إلّا أنَّهم شَدَّدُوا النُّونَ. وقَرَأ أبُو رَجاءٍ، وأبُو عُثْمانَ النَّهْدِيُّ، والنَّخَعِيُّ، والجَحْدَرِيُّ: ( تُصْحَبُنِي ) بِضَمِّ التّاءِ وكَسْرِ الحاءِ وسُكُونِ الصّادِ والباءِ. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: فِيهِما وجْهانِ:

أحَدُهُما: لا تُتابِعْنِي في شَيْءٍ ألْتَمِسُهُ مِنكَ، يُقالُ: قَدْ أصْحَبَ المُهْرُ: إذا انْقادَ.

والثّانِي: لا تَصْحَبْنِي عِلْمًا مِن عِلْمِكَ.

﴿قَدْ بَلَغْتَ مِن لَدُنِّي عُذْرًا﴾. قَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ، وأبُو عَمْرٍو، وابْنُ عامِرٍ، وحَمْزَةُ، والكِسائِيُّ: ( مِن لَدُنِّي ) مُثَقَّلٌ. وقَرَأ نافِعٌ: ( مِن لَدُنِّي ) بِضَمِّ الدّالِ مَعَ تَخْفِيفِ النُّونِ. ورَوى أبُو بَكْرٍ عَنْ عاصِمٍ: ( مِن لَدْنِي ) بِفَتْحِ اللّامِ مَعَ تَسْكِينِ الدّالِ. وفي رِوايَةٍ أُخْرى عَنْ عاصِمٍ ( لُدْنِي ) بِضَمِّ اللّامِ وتَسْكِينِ الدّالِ. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: وأجْوَدُها تَشْدِيدُ النُّونِ؛ لِأنَّ أصْلَ ( لَدُنْ ) الإسْكانُ، فَإذا أضَفْتَها إلى نَفْسِكَ زِدْتَ نُونًا، لِيَسْلَمَ سُكُونُ النُّونِ الأُولى، تَقُولُ: مِن لَدُنْ زَيْدٍ، فَتَسْكُنُ النُّونُ ثُمَّ تُضِيفُ إلى نَفْسِكَ فَتَقُولُ: مِن لَدُنِّي، كَما تَقُولُ: عَنْ زَيْدٍ وعَنِّي. فَأمّا إسْكانُ دالِ ( لَدْنِي ) فَإنَّهم أسْكَنُوها، كَما تَقُولُ في عَضُدٍ: عَضْدٍ، فَيَحْذِفُونَ الضَّمَّ. قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: يُرِيدُ: إنَّكَ قَدْ أُعْذِرْتَ فِيما بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكَ، يَعْنِي: أنَّكَ قَدْ أخْبَرْتَنِي أنِّي لا أسْتَطِيعُ مَعَكَ صَبْرًا.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فانْطَلَقا حَتّى إذا أتَيا أهْلَ قَرْيَةٍ﴾ فِيها ثَلاثَةُ أقْوالٍ:

أحَدُها: أنَّها أنْطاكِيَّةُ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ. والثّانِي: الأُبُلَّةُ، قالَهُ ابْنُ سِيرِينَ. والثّالِثُ: باجَرُوانُ، قالَهُ مُقاتِلٌ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿اسْتَطْعَما أهْلَها﴾؛ أيْ: سَألاهُمُ الضِّيافَةَ، ﴿فَأبَوْا أنْ يُضَيِّفُوهُما﴾. رَوى المُفَضَّلُ عَنْ عاصِمٍ: ( يُضَيِّفُوهُما ) بِضَمِّ الياءِ الأُولى وكَسْرِ الضّادِ وتَخْفِيفِ الياءِ الثّانِيَةِ. وقَرَأ أبُو الجَوْزاءِ كَذَلِكَ، إلّا أنَّهُ فَتَحَ الياءَ [الأُولى]. وقَرَأ الباقُونَ: ( يُضَيِّفُوهُما ) بِفَتْحِ الضّادِ وتَشْدِيدِ الياءِ الثّانِيَةِ وكَسْرِها. قالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: ومَعْنى ﴿يُضَيِّفُوهُما﴾: يُنْزِلُوهُما مَنزِلَ الأضْيافِ، يُقالُ: ضِفْتُ أنا، وأضافَنِي الَّذِي يُنْزِلُنِي. وقالَ الزَّجّاجُ: يُقالُ: ضِفْتُ الرَّجُلَ: إذا نَزَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ، وأضَفْتُهُ: إذا أنْزَلْتُهُ وقَرَيْتُهُ. وقالَ ابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ: [يُقالُ]: ضَيَّفْتُ الرَّجُلَ: إذا أنْزَلْتُهُ مَنزِلَةَ الأضْيافِ، ومِنهُ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ، وأضَفْتُهُ: أنْزَلْتُهُ، وضِفْتُهُ: نَزَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ. ورَوى أُبَيُّ بْنُ كَعْبٍ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللهِ (ﷺ)، قالَ: «كانُوا أهْلَ قَرْيَةٍ لِئامًا».

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَوَجَدا فِيها جِدارًا﴾؛ أيْ: حائِطًا. قالَ ابْنُ فارِسٍ: وجَمْعُهُ جُدُرٌ، والجُدُرُ: أصْلُ الحائِطِ. ومِنهُ حَدِيثُ الزُّبَيْرِ: «ثُمَّ دَعِ الماءَ يَرْجِعُ إلى الجَدْرِ»، والجَيْدَرُ: القَصِيرُ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿يُرِيدُ أنْ يَنْقَضَّ﴾. وقَرَأ أُبَيُّ بْنُ كَعْبٍ وأبُو رَجاءٍ: ( يَنْقاضُ ) بِألِفٍ مَمْدُودَةٍ وضادٍ مُعْجَمَةٍ. وقَرَأ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، وأبُو العالِيَةِ، وأبُو عُثْمانَ النَّهْدِيُّ: ( يَنْقاصُ ) بِألِفٍ ومَدَّةٍ وصادٍ غَيْرِ مُعْجَمَةٍ، وكُلُّهُ بِلا تَشْدِيدٍ. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: فَمَعْنى يَنْقُضُ: يَسْقُطُ بِسُرْعَةٍ، ويَنْقاصُ غَيْرُ مُعْجَمَةٍ: يَنْشَقُّ طُولًا، يُقالُ: انْقاصَتْ سِنُّهُ: إذا انْشَقَّتْ. قالَ ابْنُ مُقْسِمٍ: انْقاصَتْ سِنُّهُ، وانْقاضَتْ - بِالصّادِ والضّادِ - عَلى مَعْنًى واحِدٍ.

فَإنْ قِيلَ: كَيْفَ نُسِبَتِ الإرادَةُ إلى ما لا يَعْقِلُ؟

فالجَوابُ: أنَّ هَذا عَلى وجْهِ المَجازِ تَشْبِيهًا بِمَن يَعْقِلُ، ويُرِيدُ: لِأنَّ هَيْأتَهُ في التَّهَيُّؤِ لِلْوُقُوعِ قَدْ ظَهَرَتْ كَما يَظْهَرُ مِن أفْعالِ المُرِيدِينَ القاصِدِينَ، فَوُصِفَ بِالإرادَةِ؛ إذْ كانَتِ الصُّورَتانِ واحِدَةً، وقَدْ أضافَتِ العَرَبُ الأفْعالَ إلى ما لا يَعْقِلُ تَجَوُّزًا، قالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وجَلَّ: ﴿وَلَمّا سَكَتَ عَنْ مُوسى الغَضَبُ﴾ [الأعْرافِ: ١٥٤]، والغَضَبُ لا يَسْكُتُ، وإنَّما يَسْكُتُ صاحِبُهُ، وقالَ: ﴿فَإذا عَزَمَ الأمْرُ﴾ [مُحَمَّدٍ: ٢١]، وأنْشَدُوا مِن ذَلِكَ:

إنَّ دَهْرًا يَلُفُّ شَمْلِي بِجُمَلٍ ∗∗∗ لِزَمانٍ يَهُمُّ بِالإحْسانِ

وَقالَ آخَرُ:

يُرِيدُ الرُّمْحُ صَدْرَ أبِي بَراءٍ ∗∗∗ ويَرْغَبُ عَنْ دِماءِ بَنِي عَقِيلِ

وَقالَ آخَرُ:

ضَحِكُوا والدَّهْرُ عَنْهم ساكِتٌ ∗∗∗ ثُمَّ أبْكاهم دَمًا لَمّا نَطَقَ

وَقالَ آخَرُ:

يَشْكُو إلَيَّ جَمَلِي طُولَ السَّرى ∗∗∗ صَبْرًا جَمِيلًا فَكِلانا مُبْتَلى

وَهَذا كَثِيرٌ في أشْعارِهِمْ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَأقامَهُ﴾؛ أيْ: سَوّاهُ؛ لِأنَّهُ وجَدَهُ مائِلًا.

وَفِي كَيْفِيَّةِ ما فَعَلَ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُ دَفَعَهُ بِيَدِهِ فَقامَ. والثّانِي: هَدَمَهُ ثُمَّ قَعَدَ يَبْنِيهِ، رُوِيَ القَوْلانِ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لَوْ شِئْتَ لاتَّخَذْتَ عَلَيْهِ أجْرًا﴾. قَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ وأبُو عَمْرٍو: ( لَتَخِذْتَ ) بِكَسْرِ الخاءِ، غَيْرَ أنَّ أبا عَمْرٍو كانَ يُدْغِمُ الذّالَ، وابْنُ كَثِيرٍ يُظْهِرُها. وقَرَأ نافِعٌ، وعاصِمٌ، وابْنُ عامِرٍ، وحَمْزَةُ، والكِسائِيُّ: ( لاتَّخَذْتَ ) وكُلُّهم أدْغَمُوا، إلّا حَفْصًا عَنْ عاصِمٍ، فَإنَّهُ لَمْ يُدْغِمْ مِثْلَ ابْنِ كَثِيرٍ. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: يُقالُ: تَخِذَ يَتَّخِذُ في مَعْنى: اتَّخَذَ يَتَّخِذُ. وإنَّما قالَ لَهُ هَذا؛ لِأنَّهم لَمْ يُضَيِّفُوهُما.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿قالَ﴾ يَعْنِي: الخَضِرَ، ﴿هَذا﴾ يَعْنِي: الإنْكارَ عَلَيَّ، ﴿فِراقُ بَيْنِي وبَيْنِكَ﴾؛ أيْ: هو المُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَنا. قالَ الزَّجّاجُ: المَعْنى: هَذا فِراقٌ بَيْنِنا؛ أيْ: فِراقُ اتِّصالِنا، وكَرَّرَ ( بَيْنَ ) تَوْكِيدًا، ومِثْلُهُ في الكَلامِ: أخْزى اللَّهُ الكاذِبَ مِنِّي ومِنكَ. وقَرَأ أبُو رَزِينٍ، وابْنُ السَّمَيْفَعِ، وأبُو العالِيَةِ، وابْنُ أبِي عَبْلَةَ: ( هَذا فِراقٌ ) بِالتَّنْوِينِ ( بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكَ ) بِنَصْبِ النُّونِ. قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: كانَ قَوْلُ مُوسى في السَّفِينَةِ والغُلامِ لِرَبِّهِ، وكانَ قَوْلُهُ في الجِدارِ لِنَفْسِهِ، لِطَلَبِ شَيْءٍ مِن الدُّنْيا.

﴿Then it was for the poor﴾. Regarding what is meant by their "poverty" (maskanatihim), there are two views:

One: they were weak in their earnings. The second: they were weak in their bodies. Ka'b said: it belonged to ten brothers, five of them disabled and five of them working at sea.

﴿So I wanted to damage it﴾: that is, to make it defective, meaning by piercing it. ﴿And there was behind them﴾: regarding this there are two views.

One: "in front of them." This is said by Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, Abu 'Ubaydah and Ibn Qutaybah. Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud recited: "and there was in front of them a king."

The second: "behind them." Al-Zajjaj said: this is the better of the two views. It is possible that their return on their route was along that way, and they did not know of his news, so God Most High informed al-Khidr of his news. (p-179)

﴿Who seizes every boat by force﴾: that is, every sound boat. In the recitation of Ubayy [ibn Ka'b]: "every sound boat." Al-Khidr said: "I only damaged it because the king, when he saw it damaged, would leave it, and its people would patch it and benefit from it."

﴿As for the boy﴾: it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite: "As for the boy, he was a disbeliever." Ubayy ibn Ka'b narrated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "The boy whom al-Khidr killed was created a disbeliever, and had he lived he would have burdened his parents with rebellion and disbelief." Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: the boy was on the road, and no one passed by him without him killing or seizing from him, so his parents would supplicate against him and against themselves. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: the boy was a thief; when someone came seeking him, his parents would swear that he had not done it.

﴿So we feared﴾: regarding the one who says this, there are two views.

One: God, Mighty and Majestic. Then regarding the meaning of "fear" attributed to Him, there are two views: One is that it means "knowledge." Al-Farra' said: its meaning is "so we knew." Ibn 'Aqil said: the meaning is: our act was the act of one who fears. The second is "aversion," said by al-Akhfash and al-Zajjaj.

The second: it is al-Khidr, so "fear" means fear of a matter that is imagined. This is said by Ibn al-Anbari. Some have argued that it is from the speech of al-Khidr by His saying: ﴿So we wished that their Lord would replace them﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: "so God wished," because the wording of reports about God Most High in this manner is more than can be counted. The meaning of ﴿would burden them﴾ is: would cause them to be overtaken by ruin (rahaq), which is ignorance. Abu 'Ubaydah said: ﴿would burden them﴾ means: would overwhelm them. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "we feared (p-180) that his love would lead them to enter into his religion." Al-Zajjaj said: they rejoiced at him when he was born, and grieved over him when he was killed; had he lived, their ruin would have been in him. A man should be content with God's decree, for God's decree concerning the believer in what he dislikes is better for him than His decree concerning what he loves.

﴿So we wished that their Lord would replace them﴾: Ibn Kathir and Abu Bakr, from 'Asim, recited "an yubdilahuma" with light (tashdid-less) pronunciation. Nafi' and Abu 'Amr recited it with emphasis (tashdid).

﴿Better than him in purity﴾: regarding it there are three views.

One: in religion, said by Ibn 'Abbas. The second: in deeds, said by Muqatil. The third: in righteousness, said by al-Farra'.

﴿And nearer in kinship﴾: Ibn Kathir, Nafi', 'Asim, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited "rahiman" with the ha' unvoweled (ruhman/rahman form). Ibn 'Amir recited "rahiman" with emphasis. One: "I join the ties of kinship and I am dutiful to the parents." This is said by Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah. Al-Zajjaj said: "more inclined in affection and closer in kinship." The meaning of ruhm and ruhum in the language is: tenderness and mercy. The poet said:

The second: it was a tablet of gold, on which was written: "Wonder at one who is certain of destiny yet still toils! Wonder at one who is certain of the Fire, how can he laugh! Wonder at one who believes in death, how can he rejoice! Wonder at one who is certain of provision, how can he exert himself! Wonder at one who believes in reckoning, how can he be heedless! Wonder at one who sees the world and its turning with its people, how can he feel at ease with it! I am God, there is no god but I; Muhammad is My servant and My messenger." And on the other side: "I am God; there is no god but Me alone, with no partner. I created good and evil; so blessed is the one for whom I created good and made it run through his hands, and woe to the one for whom I created evil and made it run through his hands." Ata' narrated this from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn al-Anbari said: it was called a "treasure" because of the gold, and its name was made dominant.

The third: a treasure of knowledge. Al-'Awfi narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas. Mujahid said: scrolls in which there is knowledge. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said the same. Ibn al-Anbari said: the meaning according to this view is: there was beneath it something like a treasure, because its benefit obtained quickly is better than what is gained from wealth. Al-Zajjaj said: the known usage in the language is that "kanz," when used alone, means hidden, stored wealth; when there is no wealth, one says: "he has a treasure of knowledge" or "he has a treasure of understanding." The treasure here is more akin to wealth. It is possible that the treasure was wealth, with knowledge written in it, as has been narrated; so it was both wealth and great knowledge.

﴿And their father was righteous﴾: Ibn 'Abbas said: they were preserved through the righteousness of their father, and nothing of their own righteousness is mentioned. Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, said: between them and that righteous father were seven fathers. Muqatil said: their father was a man of trustworthiness.

﴿So your Lord willed﴾: Ibn al-Anbari said: since His saying "I wished" and "we wished" could each apply to God Mighty and Majestic or to al-Khidr, He followed them with what confines the will to Him alone and removes it from others, and reveals the purpose of the first two words. He said "I wished, we wished, your Lord willed," because the Arabs prefer variation in speech over uniformity while the meanings are the same, since it is sweeter on the tongues and better in its effect on the ears. A man says: "So-and-so said to me such-and-such, and informed me of what had happened, and told me of what he had attained." As for "the age of full strength" (al-ashudd), its mention has preceded in several places [al-An'am: 152; Yusuf: 22; al-Isra': 34]. Had al-Khidr not repaired the wall, it would have collapsed, and that treasure would have been taken before the two boys reached maturity.

﴿A mercy from your Lord﴾: that is, God had mercy on them by this. ﴿And I did not do it of my own accord﴾: Qatadah said: he was a servant under command.

As for His saying: ﴿you could not﴾ (taste'): "istata'a" and "ista'a" have one meaning.

﴿Then it was for the poor﴾. Regarding what is meant by their "poverty" (maskanatihim), there are two views:

One: they were weak in their earnings. The second: they were weak in their bodies. Ka'b said: it belonged to ten brothers, five of them disabled and five of them working at sea.

﴿So I wanted to damage it﴾: that is, to make it defective, meaning by piercing it. ﴿And there was behind them﴾: regarding this there are two views.

One: "in front of them." This is said by Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, Abu 'Ubaydah and Ibn Qutaybah. Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud recited: "and there was in front of them a king."

The second: "behind them." Al-Zajjaj said: this is the better of the two views. It is possible that their return on their route was along that way, and they did not know of his news, so God Most High informed al-Khidr of his news. (p-179)

﴿Who seizes every boat by force﴾: that is, every sound boat. In the recitation of Ubayy [ibn Ka'b]: "every sound boat." Al-Khidr said: "I only damaged it because the king, when he saw it damaged, would leave it, and its people would patch it and benefit from it."

﴿As for the boy﴾: it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite: "As for the boy, he was a disbeliever." Ubayy ibn Ka'b narrated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "The boy whom al-Khidr killed was created a disbeliever, and had he lived he would have burdened his parents with rebellion and disbelief." Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: the boy was on the road, and no one passed by him without him killing or seizing from him, so his parents would supplicate against him and against themselves. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: the boy was a thief; when someone came seeking him, his parents would swear that he had not done it.

﴿So we feared﴾: regarding the one who says this, there are two views.

One: God, Mighty and Majestic. Then regarding the meaning of "fear" attributed to Him, there are two views: One is that it means "knowledge." Al-Farra' said: its meaning is "so we knew." Ibn 'Aqil said: the meaning is: our act was the act of one who fears. The second is "aversion," said by al-Akhfash and al-Zajjaj.

The second: it is al-Khidr, so "fear" means fear of a matter that is imagined. This is said by Ibn al-Anbari. Some have argued that it is from the speech of al-Khidr by His saying: ﴿So we wished that their Lord would replace them﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: "so God wished," because the wording of reports about God Most High in this manner is more than can be counted. The meaning of ﴿would burden them﴾ is: would cause them to be overtaken by ruin (rahaq), which is ignorance. Abu 'Ubaydah said: ﴿would burden them﴾ means: would overwhelm them. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "we feared (p-180) that his love would lead them to enter into his religion." Al-Zajjaj said: they rejoiced at him when he was born, and grieved over him when he was killed; had he lived, their ruin would have been in him. A man should be content with God's decree, for God's decree concerning the believer in what he dislikes is better for him than His decree concerning what he loves.

﴿So we wished that their Lord would replace them﴾: Ibn Kathir and Abu Bakr, from 'Asim, recited "an yubdilahuma" with light (tashdid-less) pronunciation. Nafi' and Abu 'Amr recited it with emphasis (tashdid).

One: in religion, said by Ibn 'Abbas. The second: in deeds, said by Muqatil. The third: in righteousness, said by al-Farra'.

From Abu 'Amr there are two readings like these. Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Jubayr and Abu Raja' recited "rahiman" with fatha on the ra' and kasra on the ha'.

Regarding the meaning of the speech there are two views:

One: "I join the ties of kinship and I am dutiful to the parents." This is said by Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah. Al-Zajjaj said: "more inclined in affection and closer in kinship." The meaning of ruhm and ruhum in the language is: tenderness and mercy. The poet said:

"How can one wrong a maiden, when gentleness and mercy are in her?"

The second: "closer that they should be shown mercy by it," said by al-Farra'. Regarding what they were exchanged for, there are two views: (p-181)

One: a girl. This is said by most. 'Ata' narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: God replaced them with a girl who bore seventy prophets.

The second: a Muslim boy. This is said by Ibn Juraij.

﴿As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city﴾: meaning the town mentioned in His saying: ﴿They came to the people of a town﴾. Muqatil said: their names were Asram and Sarim.

﴿And beneath it was a treasure belonging to them﴾: regarding it there are three views.

One: it was gold and silver; Abu al-Darda' narrated it from the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Al-Hasan, 'Ikrimah and Qatadah said: it was wealth.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 18, verses 83–88:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn﴾. We have already mentioned the occasion of its revelation under His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Spirit﴾ [al-Isra' 17:85].

The scholars differed about the name of Dhul-Qarnayn, giving four opinions:

The first: ʿAbd Allah. ʿAli (peace be upon him) said this. It is also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that his name was ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Dahhak. The second: al-Iskandar (Alexander), said by Wahb. The third: ʿAyyash, said by Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Husayn. The fourth: al-Saʿb ibn Jabir ibn al-Qalmas, mentioned by Ibn Abi Khaythama.

Regarding the reason he was called Dhul-Qarnayn ("the Two-Horned"), there are ten opinions:

The first: he called his people to Allah the Exalted, and they struck him on his horn and he died. He remained dead for a time, then Allah revived him, and he called them to Allah again, and they struck him on his other horn and he died. These are his two horns. ʿAli (peace be upon him) said this.

The second: he was called Dhul-Qarnayn because he traveled to the west of the sun and to its east. Abu Salih narrated this from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The third: because the two sides of his head were of copper.

The fourth: because he saw in a dream as if a cord extended from the sky to the earth and he grasped the two horns of the sun. He related this to his people, and so he was called Dhul-Qarnayn.

The fifth: because he was king of the Romans and the Persians.

The sixth: because there was something like two horns on his head. I narrated these four opinions from Wahb ibn Munabbih.

The seventh: because he had two braids of hair. This was said by al-Hasan. Ibn al-Anbari said: The Arabs call two plaits of hair ghadiratayn, jamiratayn and qarnayn. He said: As for the one who said he was called this because he was king of Persia and Rome, he said: Because they are two elevated [regions] on two sides of the earth, and they are called two horns.

The eighth: because he was noble on both sides, from a house of honorable lineage.

The ninth: because two generations of people passed away during his lifetime while he was still alive.

The tenth: because he traversed the darkness and the light. Abu Ishaq al-Thaʿlabi mentioned these last three opinions.

The scholars differed over whether he was a prophet or not, in two opinions:

One of them: he was a prophet. ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said this.

The other: he was a righteous servant, not a prophet nor a king. ʿAli (peace be upon him) said this. Wahb said: He was a king to whom no revelation was sent.

Regarding the time in which he lived, there are three opinions:

The first: he was of the early generations, from the descendants of Yafith ibn Nuh (Noah). ʿAli (peace be upon him) said this.

The second: he lived after Thamud. al-Hasan said this. It is said that his lifespan was one thousand six hundred years.

The third: [that] he lived in the interval between ʿIsa and Muhammad (may Allah's blessings and peace be upon them both). Wahb said this.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿I shall recite to you from him a mention﴾; that is, a report that contains his story. ﴿Indeed, We established him in the land﴾; that is, We made travel in it easy for him. ʿAli (peace be upon him) said: He obeyed Allah, so He subjected the clouds to him, and they carried him, and He extended for him the means, and spread light for him, so that night and day were alike to him. Mujahid said: Four people ruled the earth, two believers and two disbelievers. The two believers were Sulayman ibn Dawud and Dhul-Qarnayn; the two disbelievers were Nimrod and Bukhtnassar.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We gave him of everything a means﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Knowledge by which he could attain whatever he wished. It was also said: it is knowledge of the roads and paths.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So he followed a way﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ and Abu ʿAmr recited (fa-atbaʿa sababan), (thumma atbaʿa sababan), (thumma attabaʿa sababan) with the letter taʾ doubled. ʿAsim, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited (fa-atbaʿa sababan), (thumma atbaʿa sababan), (thumma atbaʿa sababan) without doubling. Ibn al-Anbari said: Whoever recites (fa-atbaʿa sababan) its meaning is "he followed the trace." Whoever recites (fa-atbaʿa) its meaning is "he caught up," as one says: ittabaʿani fulan, meaning "so-and-so followed me," just as one says: alhaqani fulan, meaning "so-and-so caught up with me." Abu ʿAli said: The construction (atbaʿa) is to be understood as: atbaʿa sababan sababan, i.e., he followed a means after a means, and the "means" here is the road. The meaning is: he followed a road that led him to the west of the sun. Whenever he prevailed over a people, he took from them an army, and went with them to others.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Until, when he reached the setting place of the sun, he found it setting in a murky spring﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr and Hafs from ʿAsim recited (ḥamiʾatin) [with a hamza], and this is the recitation of Ibn ʿAbbas. Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim recited (ḥamiyatin) [without a hamza], and this is the recitation of ʿAmr, ʿAli, Ibn Masʿud, al-Zubayr, Muʿawiya, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, al-Hasan, ʿIkrima, al-Nakhaʿi, Qatada, Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, Ibn Muhaysin, and al-Aʿmash, all of whom did not use a hamza. Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever recites (ḥamiʾatan) intends: in a spring that has black mud. One says: ḥamaʾat al-bi'r when you removed its mud, and aḥmaʾtuha when you cast mud into it. And (ḥamiʾat) [i.e., it became muddy] and so it is ḥamiʾa when mud has settled in it. Whoever recites (ḥamiyatan) without a hamza intends: hot. It may be both hot and muddy. Qatada narrated from al-Hasan that he said: (He found it setting in water boiling like the boiling of cauldrons), and (He found near it a people) whose clothing was the skins of beasts of prey, and who had no food except what the sun had burned of the creatures when it set toward them, and what the spring cast out of the fish when the sun fell into it. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: He found near it a people, believers and disbelievers, meaning: near the spring. Some may imagine that this sun, despite its great size, sinks in its essence into a spring of water, but that is not so, for it is many times larger than this world. How then could a spring of water contain it? It was said: the sun is one hundred and fifty times the size of this world, and it was said: one hundred and twenty times, and the moon is eighty times the size of this world. He found it setting in the spring just as the rider of the sea, who cannot see its far shore, sees the sun setting into the water. That is because Dhul-Qarnayn reached the end of the inhabited lands, and found a murky spring beyond which there was no one.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿We said: O Dhul-Qarnayn!﴾ Whoever said he was a prophet said: this statement was revelation. Whoever said he was not a prophet said: this was inspiration.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Either you punish﴾. The exegetes said: either you kill them if they refuse what you call them to, or you take them captive and make them see the right path. ﴿He said: As for him who wrongs﴾; that is, who associates partners with Allah, ﴿we shall punish him﴾ by killing if he does not turn back from polytheism. al-Hasan said: He used to boil them in cauldrons. ﴿Then he will be returned to his Lord﴾ after the punishment, ﴿and He will punish him with a terrible punishment﴾ by the Fire.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿But as for him who believes and does righteous deeds, he shall have a good reward﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim recited (jazaʾu al-husna) with the noun in the nominative (raf'), with an annexed construction. al-Farra' said: (al-husna) is Paradise, and the reward is attributed to it, and it is the reward itself, as in His saying: ﴿And indeed it is the truth of certainty﴾ [al-Haqqah 69:51], ﴿the correct religion﴾ [al-Bayyinah 98:5], and ﴿and the home of the Hereafter﴾ [al-Nahl 16:30]. Abu ʿAli al-Farisi said: The meaning is: he shall have as reward the good qualities, because faith and righteous deeds are qualities. Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Hafs from ʿAsim, Khalaf and Yaʿqub recited (jazaʾan) with the accusative (nasb) and tanwin. al-Zajjaj said: It is a verbal noun in the accusative of circumstance, meaning: for him is the good, rewarding with it a reward. Ibn al-Anbari said: The reward may be other than the good, when the reward is interpreted as meaning reward (thawab), and the good is the good deed earned in this world, so the meaning is: for him is the reward for the good deeds he has sent forward.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We shall speak to him from Our command with ease﴾; that is, We shall speak to him a gentle word.

Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim recited (ḥamiyatin) [without a hamza], and this is the recitation of ʿAmr, ʿAli, Ibn Masʿud, al-Zubayr, Muʿawiya, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, al-Hasan, ʿIkrima, al-Nakhaʿi, Qatada, Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, Ibn Muhaysin, and al-Aʿmash, all of whom did not use a hamza. Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever recites (ḥamiʾatan) intends: in a spring that has black mud. One says: ḥamaʾat al-bi'r when you removed its mud, and aḥmaʾtuha when you cast mud into it. And (ḥamiʾat) [i.e., it became muddy] and so it is ḥamiʾa when mud has settled in it. Whoever recites (ḥamiyatan) without a hamza intends: hot. It may be both hot and muddy. Qatada narrated from al-Hasan that he said: (He found it setting in water boiling like the boiling of cauldrons), and (He found near it a people) whose clothing was the skins of beasts of prey, and who had no food except what the sun had burned of the creatures when it set toward them, and what the spring cast out of the fish when the sun fell into it. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: He found near it a people, believers and disbelievers, meaning: near the spring. Some may imagine that this sun, despite its great size, sinks in its essence into a spring of water, but that is not so, for it is many times larger than this world. How then could a spring of water contain it? It was said: the sun is one hundred and fifty times the size of this world, and it was said: one hundred and twenty times, and the moon is eighty times the size of this world. He found it setting in the spring just as the rider of the sea, who cannot see its far shore, sees the sun setting into the water. That is because Dhul-Qarnayn reached the end of the inhabited lands, and found a murky spring beyond which there was no one.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿We said: O Dhul-Qarnayn!﴾ Whoever said he was a prophet said: this statement was revelation. Whoever said he was not a prophet said: this was inspiration.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Either you punish﴾. The exegetes said: either you kill them if they refuse what you call them to, or you take them captive and make them see the right path. ﴿He said: As for him who wrongs﴾; that is, who associates partners with Allah, ﴿we shall punish him﴾ by killing if he does not turn back from polytheism. al-Hasan said: He used to boil them in cauldrons. ﴿Then he will be returned to his Lord﴾ after the punishment, ﴿and He will punish him with a terrible punishment﴾ by the Fire.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿But as for him who believes and does righteous deeds, he shall have a good reward﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim recited (jazaʾu al-husna) with the noun in the nominative (raf'), with an annexed construction. al-Farra' said: (al-husna) is Paradise, and the reward is attributed to it, and it is the reward itself, as in His saying: ﴿And indeed it is the truth of certainty﴾ [al-Haqqah 69:51], ﴿the correct religion﴾ [al-Bayyinah 98:5], and ﴿and the home of the Hereafter﴾ [al-Nahl 16:30]. Abu ʿAli al-Farisi said: The meaning is: he shall have as reward the good qualities, because faith and righteous deeds are qualities. Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Hafs from ʿAsim, Khalaf and Yaʿqub recited (jazaʾan) with the accusative (nasb) and tanwin. al-Zajjaj said: It is a verbal noun in the accusative of circumstance, meaning: for him is the good, rewarding with it a reward. Ibn al-Anbari said: The reward may be other than the good, when the reward is interpreted as meaning reward (thawab), and the good is the good deed earned in this world, so the meaning is: for him is the reward for the good deeds he has sent forward.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We shall speak to him from Our command with ease﴾; that is, We shall speak to him a gentle word.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 18, verses 83–88:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn﴾. We have already mentioned the occasion of its revelation under His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Spirit﴾ [al-Isra' 17:85].

The scholars differed about the name of Dhul-Qarnayn, giving four opinions:

The first: ʿAbd Allah. ʿAli (peace be upon him) said this. It is also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that his name was ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Dahhak. The second: al-Iskandar (Alexander), said by Wahb. The third: ʿAyyash, said by Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Husayn. The fourth: al-Saʿb ibn Jabir ibn al-Qalmas, mentioned by Ibn Abi Khaythama.

Regarding the reason he was called Dhul-Qarnayn ("the Two-Horned"), there are ten opinions:

The first: he called his people to Allah the Exalted, and they struck him on his horn and he died. He remained dead for a time, then Allah revived him, and he called them to Allah again, and they struck him on his other horn and he died. These are his two horns. ʿAli (peace be upon him) said this.

The second: he was called Dhul-Qarnayn because he traveled to the west of the sun and to its east. Abu Salih narrated this from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The third: because the two sides of his head were of copper.

The fourth: because he saw in a dream as if a cord extended from the sky to the earth and he grasped the two horns of the sun. He related this to his people, and so he was called Dhul-Qarnayn.

The fifth: because he was king of the Romans and the Persians.

The sixth: because there was something like two horns on his head. I narrated these four opinions from Wahb ibn Munabbih.

The seventh: because he had two braids of hair. This was said by al-Hasan. Ibn al-Anbari said: The Arabs call two plaits of hair ghadiratayn, jamiratayn and qarnayn. He said: As for the one who said he was called this because he was king of Persia and Rome, he said: Because they are two elevated [regions] on two sides of the earth, and they are called two horns.

The eighth: because he was noble on both sides, from a house of honorable lineage.

The ninth: because two generations of people passed away during his lifetime while he was still alive.

The tenth: because he traversed the darkness and the light. Abu Ishaq al-Thaʿlabi mentioned these last three opinions.

The scholars differed over whether he was a prophet or not, in two opinions:

One of them: he was a prophet. ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said this.

The other: he was a righteous servant, not a prophet nor a king. ʿAli (peace be upon him) said this. Wahb said: He was a king to whom no revelation was sent.

Regarding the time in which he lived, there are three opinions:

The first: he was of the early generations, from the descendants of Yafith ibn Nuh (Noah). ʿAli (peace be upon him) said this.

The second: he lived after Thamud. al-Hasan said this. It is said that his lifespan was one thousand six hundred years.

The third: [that] he lived in the interval between ʿIsa and Muhammad (may Allah's blessings and peace be upon them both). Wahb said this.

Mujahid said: Four people ruled the earth, two believers and two disbelievers. The two believers were Sulayman ibn Dawud and Dhul-Qarnayn; the two disbelievers were Nimrod and Bukhtnassar.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We gave him of everything a means﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Knowledge by which he could attain whatever he wished. It was also said: it is knowledge of the roads and paths.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So he followed a way﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ and Abu ʿAmr recited (fa-atbaʿa sababan), (thumma atbaʿa sababan), (thumma attabaʿa sababan) with the letter taʾ doubled. ʿAsim, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited (fa-atbaʿa sababan), (thumma atbaʿa sababan), (thumma atbaʿa sababan) without doubling. Ibn al-Anbari said: Whoever recites (fa-atbaʿa sababan) its meaning is "he followed the trace." Whoever recites (fa-atbaʿa) its meaning is "he caught up," as one says: ittabaʿani fulan, meaning "so-and-so followed me," just as one says: alhaqani fulan, meaning "so-and-so caught up with me." Abu ʿAli said: The construction (atbaʿa) is to be understood as: atbaʿa sababan sababan, i.e., he followed a means after a means, and the "means" here is the road. The meaning is: he followed a road that led him to the west of the sun. Whenever he prevailed over a people, he took from them an army, and went with them to others.

Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr and Hafs from ʿAsim recited (ḥamiʾatin) [with a hamza], and this is the recitation of Ibn ʿAbbas. Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 18, verse 89–91:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then he followed a way﴾ (sababan); that is, another route that brought him to the east. Qatadah said: He proceeded, conquering cities, gathering treasures, and killing men, except those who believed, until he reached the rising place of the sun, and he found a people in caves, naked, who had no food except what the sun scorched when it rose; and when it reached the middle of the sky, they came out of their caves seeking their livelihood from what the sun had scorched. It has reached us that they were in a place on which no building would stand, and it is said that they were the Zanj. Al-Hasan said: When the sun set, they would come out peering at one another as wild beasts peer.

Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Abu Mijlaz, Abu Rajaa, and Ibn Muhaysin read (matli'i ash-shams) with a fatha on the lam. Ibn al-Anbari said: There is no disagreement among the people of Arabic grammar that al-mat'li (with kasra) and al-matla' (with fatha) both refer to the place from which the sun rises. They say: whatever is on the pattern fa'ala yaf'ulu, the verbal noun and the noun of place come on the pattern mafal, like their saying: al-mudkhal (the entrance) for entering, and the place from which one enters. Except for eleven words which came with a kasra when the places are meant, and they are: al-matli' (the rising place), al-maskin (the dwelling), al-mansik (the place of rites), al-mashriq (the place of rising), al-maghrib (the place of setting), al-masjid (the place of prostration), al-manbit (the place of growth), al-majzir (the slaughterhouse), al-mafriq (the parting place), al-masqit (the place of falling), and al-mahbil (the place where the she-camel gives birth). Five of these eleven words are heard with both kasra and fatha: al-matla' and al-matli', al-mansak and al-mansik, al-majzar and al-majzir, al-maskan and al-maskin, and al-manbat and al-manbit. Al-Hasan read according to the original form, admitting the two described vowelings of the pattern mafal [with fatha and kasra of the ayn]; the reading of the majority follows the usage of the Arabs and what is common on their tongues, and they assigned the kasra to the place and preferred the fatha for the verbal noun. Abu Amr said: (al-matli') with kasra is the place where one rises, and (al-matla') with fatha is the act of rising. Ibn al-Anbari said: This is the original usage; then the Arabs extend their usage, making the noun stand in for the verbal noun, so they read (hatta matli'i al-fajr) [al-Qadr: 5] with kasra, and they mean the rising; and whoever reads (matla'a ash-shams) with fatha does so on the basis that it is a place, in the same position as al-madkhal, which is a noun for the place from which one enters.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Thus﴾ (kadhalika). Concerning it there are four opinions:

The first: Just as he reached the setting place of the sun, he reached its rising place.

The second: He followed a way just as he had followed a way.

The third: Just as he found those people at the setting of the sun and judged them, so he found these people at its rising and judged them.

The fourth: The meaning is: Thus did He command him, as We have related to you. Then He resumed, saying: ﴿And We had comprehensive knowledge of what was before him﴾; that is, of what was with him and in his company of armies and equipment. Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi related: ﴿what was before him﴾, that is, what was at the rising place of the sun. The meaning of this statement has already passed [al-Kahf: 68].

**Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on Surah 18, verses 92–98:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then he followed a way﴾; that is, a third route between the east and the west. ﴿Until, when he reached between the two barriers﴾. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "They are two lofty mountains in the sky. Behind them is the sea, and in front of them are the lands. They lie at the edge of the land of the Turks, on the side that adjoins the country of Armenia." ʿAtaʾ al-Khurasani narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The two mountains are on the side of Armenia and Adharbayjan."

The reciters differed over the word "al-saddayn" (the two barriers). Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, and Hafs from ʿAsim read it with a fatha on the sin (السَّدَّيْنِ). Nafiʿ, Ibn ʿAmir, Abu Bakr from ʿAsim, Hamzah, and al-Kisaʾi read it with a damma on the sin (السُّدَّيْنِ).

Is the meaning the same or not? There are two opinions on this:

The first: it has one meaning. Ibn al-Aʿrabi said: "Whatever stands opposite you and blocks what is behind it is a *sadd* and a *sudd*, like *al-daʿf* and *al-duʿf* (weakness), and *al-faqr* and *al-fuqr* (poverty)." Al-Kisaʾi and Thaʿlab said: "*Al-sadd* and *al-sudd* are two dialects with one meaning." This is also the view of al-Zajjaj.

The second: they differ in meaning.

Regarding the distinction between them, there are two opinions:

The first: what is the work of God, Exalted is He, is pronounced with a damma, and what is the work of human beings is pronounced with a fatha. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿIkrimah, and Abu ʿUbaydah. Al-Farraʾ said: "On this view I have seen the elders and the scholars among the grammarians."

The second: *al-sadd* with a fatha on the sin means the barrier between two things, while *al-sudd* with a damma means a film over the eye. This was said by Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿he found beside them a people who scarcely understood any speech﴾. That is, in front of the two barriers. Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, ʿAsim, and Ibn ʿAmir read *yafqahuna qawlan* (يَفْقَهُونَ قَوْلا) with a fatha on the ya, meaning: they scarcely understand it. Ibn al-Anbari said: "The linguists said its meaning is that they understand after delay, like His saying: ﴿and they almost did not do it﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:71]." The exegetes said: "They were like this only because they did not know any language other than their own." Hamzah and al-Kisaʾi read *yufqihuna* (يُفْقِهُونَ) with a damma on the ya, meaning: they make others understand. It was also said that interpreters spoke to Dhu al-Qarnayn on their behalf.

The second: it is molten iron. This was said by Abu ʿUbaydah.

The third: it is melted brass. This was said by Muqatil.

The fourth: it is lead. This was related by Ibn al-Anbari.

They return to it and it is in the same state as when they left it, so they dig through it and come out against the people." He mentioned the rest of the hadith. I have mentioned this hadith in full and others like it in my book *al-Ḥadāʾiq*, so I disliked lengthening it here.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He said: "This is a mercy from my Lord"﴾. When Dhu al-Qarnayn finished its building, he said this. Regarding what he referred to, there are two opinions:

The first: it is the barrier. This was said by Muqatil. He said: the meaning is: this is a blessing from my Lord upon the Muslims, so that they do not go out to them.

The second: it is the empowerment by which he accomplished the work of the barrier. This was said by al-Zajjaj.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So when the promise of my Lord comes﴾. There are two opinions regarding this:

The first: it is the Resurrection.

The second: it is His promise of the emergence of Gog and Magog.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He will make it level﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿAmir read *dakkan* (دَكًّا) with tanwin, without hamzah and without a long vowel. ʿAsim, Hamzah, and al-Kisaʾi read *dakkāʾa* (دَكّاءَ) with a long vowel and a hamzah, without tanwin. We have explained the meaning of this word in *al-Aʿrāf* (7:143).

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the promise of my Lord is ever true﴾, that is, with regard to reward and punishment.

Abu al-Jawzaʾ, Abu ʿImran, al-Zuhri, and al-Jahdari read it with a damma on the sad and a fatha on the dal. Ibn al-Anbari said: "It is said *sadafa*, on the pattern of *naghara*, and all of these are dialects of the word." Abu ʿUbaydah said: "*Al-Sadafan* are the two sides of a mountain." Al-Azhari said: "The two sides of a mountain are called *sadafan* when they face each other, because they meet (*tasadafa*), that is, they encounter each other."

The exegetes said: he filled the space between the two mountains with iron, and he arranged between the layers of iron wood and charcoal, and he placed bellows over them. Then ﴿he said: "Blow"﴾, and they blew, ﴿until, when he had made it﴾, that is, the iron. It was also said that the pronoun refers to what is between the two cliffs, ﴿fire﴾, that is, like fire, because iron, when heated with charcoal and bellows, becomes like fire. ﴿He said: "Bring me"﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir, and al-Kisaʾi read *ʾātūnī* (آَتَوْنِي) with a long vowel, meaning: give me. Hamzah and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim read *ʾītūnī* (إيتُونِي) with a short vowel, meaning: bring it to me, "I will pour it over it."

There are four opinions regarding *al-qiṭr* (القِطْر):

The first: it is copper. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Farraʾ, and al-Zajjaj.

The second: it is molten iron. This was said by Abu ʿUbaydah.

The third: it is melted brass. This was said by Muqatil.

The fourth: it is lead. This was related by Ibn al-Anbari.

The exegetes said: he melted the *qiṭr* and poured it over the iron, and it mixed and stuck together until it became a solid mountain of iron and copper. Qatadah said: "It was like striped cloth, with a black streak and a red streak."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿so they could not﴾. The original is *fa-mā istaṭāʿū* (فَما اسْتَطاعُوا). Because the tāʾ and the ṭāʾ come from the same point of articulation, they preferred lightening and dropped one. Ibn al-Anbari said: "The Arabs only say *istaṭāʿa* in lightened form, just as they say *sawfa yaqūmu* and *sa-yaqūmu*, dropping the fāʾ."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿to scale it﴾, that is, to climb over it. One says: "So-and-so climbed (*ẓahara*) on top of the house" when he went up on it. The meaning is: they could not climb over it because of its height and smoothness. ﴿Nor could they pierce it﴾ from its base, because of its strength and hardness.

Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Gog and Magog dig through the barrier every day, until when they almost see the rays of the sun, the one who is over them says: 'Go back, for you will dig through it tomorrow.' They return to it and find it as strong as it was. Until, when their term is complete and God, Mighty and Majestic, wills to send them out against the people, they dig until they almost see the rays of the sun, and the one over them says: 'Go back, for you will dig through it tomorrow, God willing,' and he makes the exception. They return to it and it is in the same state as when they left it, so they dig through it and come out against the people." He mentioned the rest of the hadith. I have mentioned this hadith in full and others like it in my book *al-Ḥadāʾiq*, so I disliked lengthening it here.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He said: "This is a mercy from my Lord"﴾. When Dhu al-Qarnayn finished its building, he said this. Regarding what he referred to, there are two opinions:

The first: it is the barrier. This was said by Muqatil. He said: the meaning is: this is a blessing from my Lord upon the Muslims, so that they do not go out to them.

The second: it is the empowerment by which he accomplished the work of the barrier. This was said by al-Zajjaj.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So when the promise of my Lord comes﴾. There are two opinions regarding this:

The first: it is the Resurrection.

The second: it is His promise of the emergence of Gog and Magog.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He will make it level﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿAmir read *dakkan* (دَكًّا) with tanwin, without hamzah and without a long vowel. ʿAsim, Hamzah, and al-Kisaʾi read *dakkāʾa* (دَكّاءَ) with a long vowel and a hamzah, without tanwin. We have explained the meaning of this word in *al-Aʿrāf* (7:143).

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the promise of my Lord is ever true﴾, that is, with regard to reward and punishment.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on Surah 18, verses 92–98:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then he followed a way﴾; that is, a third route between the east and the west. ﴿Until, when he reached between the two barriers﴾. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "They are two lofty mountains in the sky. Behind them is the sea, and in front of them are the lands. They lie at the edge of the land of the Turks, on the side that adjoins the country of Armenia." ʿAtaʾ al-Khurasani narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The two mountains are on the side of Armenia and Adharbayjan."

The reciters differed over the word "al-saddayn" (the two barriers). Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, and Hafs from ʿAsim read it with a fatha on the sin (السَّدَّيْنِ). Nafiʿ, Ibn ʿAmir, Abu Bakr from ʿAsim, Hamzah, and al-Kisaʾi read it with a damma on the sin (السُّدَّيْنِ).

Is the meaning the same or not? There are two opinions on this:

The first: it has one meaning. Ibn al-Aʿrabi said: "Whatever stands opposite you and blocks what is behind it is a *sadd* and a *sudd*, like *al-daʿf* and *al-duʿf* (weakness), and *al-faqr* and *al-fuqr* (poverty)." Al-Kisaʾi and Thaʿlab said: "*Al-sadd* and *al-sudd* are two dialects with one meaning." This is also the view of al-Zajjaj.

The second: they differ in meaning.

Regarding the distinction between them, there are two opinions:

The first: what is the work of God, Exalted is He, is pronounced with a damma, and what is the work of human beings is pronounced with a fatha. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿIkrimah, and Abu ʿUbaydah. Al-Farraʾ said: "On this view I have seen the elders and the scholars among the grammarians."

The second: *al-sadd* with a fatha on the sin means the barrier between two things, while *al-sudd* with a damma means a film over the eye. This was said by Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿he found beside them a people who scarcely understood any speech﴾. That is, in front of the two barriers. Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, ʿAsim, and Ibn ʿAmir read *yafqahuna qawlan* (يَفْقَهُونَ قَوْلا) with a fatha on the ya, meaning: they scarcely understand it. Ibn al-Anbari said: "The linguists said its meaning is that they understand after delay, like His saying: ﴿and they almost did not do it﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:71]." The exegetes said: "They were like this only because they did not know any language other than their own." Hamzah and al-Kisaʾi read *yufqihuna* (يُفْقِهُونَ) with a damma on the ya, meaning: they make others understand. It was also said that interpreters spoke to Dhu al-Qarnayn on their behalf.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Gog and Magog﴾. They are two non-Arabic names, and ʿAsim read them with a hamzah. Al-Layth said: "Pronouncing them with a hamzah is a poor dialect." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Yajuj is a man and Majuj is a man, and they are the two sons of Yafith son of Noah, peace be upon him. Gog and Magog are ten parts, and all the children of Adam are one part. They are a span, two spans, and three spans in height." ʿAli, peace be upon him, said: "Among them is one whose height is a span, and among them is one who is excessively tall. They have hair that shelters them from heat and cold." al-Dahhak said: "They are a generation of the Turks." al-Suddi said: "The Turks are a detachment from Gog and Magog that came out to raid. Dhu al-Qarnayn came and built the barrier, and they remained outside it."

Shaqiq narrated from Huthayfah, who said: "I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about Gog and Magog, and he said: 'Yajuj is a nation and Majuj is a nation. Each nation is four hundred [thousand] nations. No man among them dies until he sees a thousand males from his own loins before him, all of them carrying weapons.' I said: 'O Messenger of God, describe them to us.' He said: 'They are three types. One type is like the *ʾurz* (cedar).' I said: 'O Messenger of God, what is the *ʾurz*?' He said: 'A tree in Syria whose height is one hundred and twenty cubits into the sky. Another type has equal length and width, one hundred and twenty cubits, and these are the ones before whom no mountain or iron can stand. Another type has one of them spreading out one ear as a bed and covering himself with the other. They do not pass by an elephant, a wild animal, a camel, or a pig without eating it, and whoever dies among them they eat. Their vanguard is in Syria and their rear is in Khurasan. They drink the rivers of the East and the lake of Tiberias.'"

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿causing corruption in the land﴾. There are four opinions regarding this corruption:

The first: they used to do the deed of the people of Lot. This was said by Wahb ibn Munabbih.

The second: they used to eat people. This was said by Saʿid ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz.

The third: they would go out to the land of those who complained of them during the spring, and they would leave nothing green without eating it and nothing dry without carrying it off to their own land. This was said by Ibn al-Sa'ib.

The fourth: they used to kill people. This was said by Muqatil.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Shall we then pay you a tribute?﴾ Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir, and ʿAsim read *kharjan* (خَرْجًا) without an alif. Hamzah and al-Kisaʾi read *kharajan* (خَراجًا) with an alif. Is there a difference between them? There are two opinions:

The first: they are two dialects with one meaning. This was said by Abu ʿUbaydah and al-Layth.

The second: *al-kharj* is what you give voluntarily, while *al-kharaj* is what is obligatory for you to pay. This was said by Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ. The exegetes said: the meaning is: shall we bring out to you some of our wealth as a payment for you?

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿What my Lord has established me in is better﴾. Ibn Kathir read *makkananiy* (مَكَّنَنِي) with two nuns, and it is so in the codices of Makkah. Al-Zajjaj said: "Whoever reads *makkanniy* (مَكَّنِّي) with the shadda assimilates the first nun into the second because of the meeting of two nuns. Regarding what he meant by the empowerment given to him, there are two opinions:

The first: it is knowledge of God and seeking His reward.

The second: it is what he possessed of the world. The meaning is: what God has given me is better than what you offer me.

The first: it means men. This was said by Mujahid and Muqatil.

The second: it means tools. This was said by Ibn al-Sa'ib. As for *al-radm* (الرَّدْمُ), it is the barrier. Al-Zajjaj said: "In the language *al-radm* is larger than *al-sadd*, because *al-radm* is what is made by placing some parts over others. The meaning is: they brought them to him and he built it. ﴿Until, when he had leveled [them] between the two cliffs﴾. Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 18, verse 99–101:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another﴾. Regarding those referred to, there are three opinions.

The first: they are Ya'juj and Ma'juj. Then, regarding what is meant by ﴿that day﴾, there are two views. One of them: it is the day when the matter of the barrier (sadd) ended, and they were left surging over one another behind it, mixed together because of their great number. It was also said: they surged in amazement at the barrier. The second: it is the day when they come out from the barrier, and they are left surging over one another.

The second: they are the disbelievers.

The third: they are all creation; jinn and humankind surge about bewildered. According to these two opinions, the day mentioned is the Day of Resurrection.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the Horn will be blown﴾. This is the blast of resurrection. We have already explained the meaning of ﴿the Horn (ṣūr)﴾ in (al-An'am: 73).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We will present Hell﴾; that is, We will make it manifest to them so that they witness it.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those whose eyes were under a covering﴾, meaning: the eyes of their hearts, ﴿in a covering﴾; that is, in heedlessness ﴿of My remembrance﴾; that is, of My oneness, and of faith in Me and in My Book. ﴿And they were unable to hear﴾: this is because of their enmity and obstinacy, and their aversion to what they are warned of, just as you say to one who dislikes your words: "You cannot even bear to hear my speech."

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 18, verse 102:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants﴾ (i.e., do the polytheists think that they may take) ﴿as protectors instead of Me?﴾ Regarding who these "servants" are, there are three opinions:

The first: they are the devils (shayatin), related by Ibn 'Abbas.
The second: they are the idols, related by Muqatil.
The third: they are the angels, the Messiah, 'Uzayr, and all other objects of worship besides Him, related by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿min duni﴾ ("instead of Me"). Nafi' and Abu 'Amr pronounced this ya' with a fatha (as "min duniya"). The answer to the interrogative in this verse is omitted, and there are two opinions regarding its implied meaning:

One of them: "Do they reckon that they may take them as protectors? By no means! Rather, they are enemies to them, and they will disavow them."

The second: "That they may take them as protectors, and I will not be angry or punish them?" Aban related from 'Asim, and Zayd from Ya'qub, the reading (afa-hasb) with the sin sukun and the ba' damma, which is the reading of 'Ali (peace be upon him), Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ibn Ya'mur, and Ibn Muhaysin. Its meaning: "Is it sufficient for them that they take them as protectors?" (p-197)

As for (nuzul) (the word "nuzul"), there are two opinions:

The first: it is what is prepared for a guest and for an army, related by Ibn Qutaybah.

The second: it is the dwelling-place (manzil), related by al-Zajjaj.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 18, verses 103–106:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in their deeds?﴾ Concerning them there are two opinions:

The first: they are the priests and the monks. This was said by Ali (peace be upon him) and al-Dahhak.

The second: they are the Jews and the Christians. This was said by Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿in deeds﴾ is in the accusative as a tamyiz (specification, a noun that clarifies an ambiguity). This is because when He said ﴿the greatest losers﴾, it was vague and did not indicate what they had lost, so it was clarified as to what kind of thing it was.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿those whose effort is lost﴾; that is, their works and their striving in this world are rendered void, while they think that they are doing good by their actions. Their leaders know the truth but prefer falsehood so that their leadership may endure, and their followers are imitators without evidence. ﴿They are those who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord﴾ denied the proofs of His oneness, and disbelieved in the Resurrection and the recompense. This is because by their disbelief in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Qur'an, they became disbelievers in these things as well. ﴿So their deeds are rendered void﴾; that is, their striving is made void because it was devoid of faith. ﴿So We shall not assign them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾. Ibn Mas'ud and al-Jahdari recited it as: (fa-la yuqimu) with the letter ya'.(p-198)

As to its meaning, there are three opinions:

The first: the scale is only made heavy by obedience, and only good deeds and bad deeds are weighed, and the disbeliever has no obedience.

The second: the meaning is: We shall not assign them any value. Ibn al-A'rabi said in explaining this verse: it is said, "Such-and-such a person has no weight with us," meaning he has no value, because of his baseness. So the meaning is that they will not be regarded, and they will have no value or standing with Allah. Abu Hurayra narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "A tall, heavy-eating, heavy-drinking man will be brought, and he will not weigh the wing of a mosquito. Recite, if you wish: ﴿So We shall not assign them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾."

The third: He said ﴿So We shall not assign them﴾ because the weighing is against them, not for them. This was mentioned by Ibn al-Anbari.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That is their recompense﴾; that is, the matter is as you have mentioned: the voiding of their deeds and the baseness of their standing. Then He began, saying: ﴿Their recompense is Hell﴾. It was also said: the meaning is: that diminishment is for them, and their recompense is Hell, so the wawu of the circumstantial clause has been omitted.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿because they disbelieved﴾; that is, because of their disbelief and their taking ﴿My signs﴾ which I revealed ﴿and My messengers in mockery﴾; that is, as things mocked at.(p-199)

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 18, verses 107–108:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿For them there will be the Gardens of Paradise (Firdaws) as a lodging﴾. Ibn al-Anbari said: "They had it in the knowledge of Allah before they were created."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Musa, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The Gardens of Firdaws are four: two of gold, their fittings and vessels and whatever is in them; and two of silver, their fittings and vessels and whatever is in them. Nothing stands between the people and looking upon their Lord except the cloak of greatness over His face, in the Garden of Eden."

Ubada ibn al-Samit narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Paradise has one hundred levels, the distance between every two levels is like the distance between the heaven and the earth. Firdaws is the highest of them, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth. So when you ask Allah, the Exalted, ask Him for Firdaws."

Abu Umama said: "Firdaws is the navel (centre) of Paradise."

Mujahid said: "Firdaws is the garden (bustan) in Roman (Greek) language."

Ka'b and al-Dahhak said: "Gardens of Firdaws: gardens of grapevines."

Al-Kalbi and al-Farra' said: "Firdaws: the garden in which there is a vineyard."

Al-Mubarrad said: "Firdaws, as far as I have heard from the speech of the Arabs: thick-entwined trees, and what predominates in it is grapes."

Tha'lab said: "Every garden that is enclosed is a firdaws." Abdullah ibn Rawaha said:

"In the gardens of Firdaws, they do not fear departing from them, nor any change."

I read to our shaikh Abu Mansur al-Lughawi, who said: al-Zajjaj said: "Firdaws is originally Roman (Greek), which was Arabized, and it means the garden; so it came in the tafsir. It has also been said: Firdaws is known to the Arabs, who call a place where there is a vineyard firdaws."

The people of lexicography said: Firdaws is masculine, but it was made feminine in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will inherit Firdaws; therein they will abide forever﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 11], because He meant by it Paradise.

Al-Zajjaj said: It has also been said: Firdaws is the valleys that grow various kinds of plants. It has also been said that it is a Roman word transferred into the Arabic form. He said: Firdaws is also in Syriac, pronounced exactly so: firdaws. He said: We did not find it in the poetry of the Arabs except in the poetry of Hassan. Its reality is that it is the garden that gathers everything that is in gardens, because among the people of every language it is so. The verse of Hassan:

"Indeed, the reward of Allah for every monotheist is gardens of Firdaws, in which he will be made eternal."

Ibn al-Kalbi said, with his chain: "Firdaws: the garden in the language of the Romans." Al-Farra' said: "It is also Arabic, and the Arabs call a garden in which there is a vineyard firdaws." Al-Suddi said: "Firdaws originally in Nabataean is (firdasan)." Abdullah ibn al-Harith said: "Firdaws: grapevines."

We have already explained the meaning of His saying: ﴿nuzulan﴾ earlier.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will not desire any change from it (lawlan)﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: They do not desire any transfer (tahawwul) from it. It is said: "He moved (hala) from his place, hawalan," just as they say of verbal nouns: "saghura saghaaran" and "adhuma adhaman" and "a'adani hubbuha 'awdan." He said: It has also been said that al-hiwal means the stratagem (hilah), so the meaning is: they do not seek a dwelling other than it.

If it is said: It is known that Paradise is abundant in goodness, so what is the point of praising it by saying they do not desire any change from it?

The answer: A person may find in a fine house some meaning that does not suit him, so he loves to move to another house, and he may become bored. But Paradise is the opposite of that.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 18, verse 109:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Even if the sea were ink for the words of my Lord﴾. The occasion of its revelation: when His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾ [al-Isra' 17:85] was revealed, the Jews said: "How, when we have been given the Torah, in which is the knowledge of everything?" So this verse was revealed. This was related by Ibn 'Abbas.

The meaning of the verse: even if the water of the sea were ink with which to write. Mujahid said: [the meaning is]: even if the sea were ink for the pen, and the pen writes. Ibn al-Anbari said: ink (midad) is so named because it supplies (imdad) the writer, and its root is from increase (ziyadah) and something coming after something.

al-Hasan and al-A'mash read: (madadan li-kalimati rabbi) without an alif.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿before the words of my Lord are exhausted﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu 'Amr and 'Asim read: (tanfada) with a ta'. Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read: (yanfada) with a ya'. Abu 'Ali said: the feminine is better, because the verb's subject is feminine; and the masculine is good, because the feminine is not real (haqiqi). The words of God are not exhausted because His speech is one of the attributes of His essence (dhat), and exhaustion (nafad) does not befall His attributes. ﴿And even if We brought the like of it﴾; that is, the like of the sea, ﴿as a supplement (madad)﴾; that is, an increase. Madad is everything that adds to something.

If it is asked: why did He say at the beginning of the verse "midadan" and at its end "madadan," when both have one meaning and their derivation is not different?

Ibn al-Anbari has answered this, saying: since the second is the end of a verse, and the verse-endings here come in the pattern of fi'l and fi'l, like His saying: ﴿nuzulan﴾, ﴿huzuwan﴾, ﴿hiwalan﴾, the word "madadan" was more similar to these words than "midad" was. The agreement of the rhyme-endings at the ends of verses, the conclusion of poetic lines, and the completion of rhymed prose is lighter on the tongues and sweeter in its effect on the ears; so the two words differed for this reason. Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Abu Raja', Qatadah and Ibn Muhaysin read: (wa-law ji'na bi-mithlihi midadan), taking it according to the first and not regarding the rhyme-endings. The reading of the first group is clearer in argument and more evident in method.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 18, verse 110:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Allah the Exalted taught His Messenger humility, lest he become conceited toward His creation, so He commanded him to acknowledge concerning himself that he is a son of Adam like others, except that he was honored with revelation.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾. The occasion of its revelation: "Jundub ibn Zuhayr al-Ghamidi said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Indeed I perform an action [for Allah, the Exalted], and when it is noticed by someone, it pleases me. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed Allah is Good and accepts only what is good, and He does not accept what is done for display,' so this verse was revealed concerning him." This was related by Ibn ʿAbbas. Tawus said: "A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: Indeed I love jihad [in the way of Allah], and I love that my position be seen, so this verse was revealed." Mujahid said: "A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: Indeed I give charity and maintain the ties of kinship, and I do that only for Allah, the Exalted; but that is mentioned about me and I am praised for it, so that pleases me and I am impressed by it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was silent, and then this verse was revealed."

Concerning His saying ﴿whoever hopes﴾ there are two views: One: he fears, related by Ibn Qutayba. The second: he hopes/aspires, which is the choice of al-Zajjaj. Ibn al-Anbari said: the meaning is: whoever hopes for the meeting with the reward of his Lord. The exegetes said: that is the Day of Resurrection and recompense. ﴿Then let him do righteous work﴾, not showing off by it, ﴿and let him not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: [it means] he does not show off. Muʿawiya ibn Abi Sufyan said: this is the last verse to be revealed from the Qur'an.
